bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation at high risk of stroke or death, rhythm-control vs rate-control showed no statistically significant difference in overall mortality (hazard ratio, 1.15 [95 percent confidence interval, 0.99 to 1.34]; P=0.08).
implications: These data support the conclusion that, in this trial population, rhythm control did not demonstrate a statistically significant survival advantage over rate control (hazard ratio 1.15 [95 percent confidence interval, 0.99 to 1.34]; P=0.08), while hospitalizations were higher with rhythm control (80.1 percent vs. 73.0 percent, P<0.001). The results do not establish equivalence or noninferiority and do not show a reduction in ischemic stroke with rhythm control (annual rate approximately 1 percent per year in each group).

major_points.text: Randomized, multicenter comparison in atrial fibrillation patients at high risk of stroke or death, with overall mortality as the primary endpoint.
major_points.quote: Methods We conducted a randomized, multicenter comparison of these two treatment strategies in patients with atrial fibrillation and a high risk of stroke or death. The primary end point was overall mortality.

major_points.text: 4060 patients were enrolled; mean age 69.7±9.0 years.
major_points.quote: A total of 4060 patients (mean [±SD] age, 69.7±9.0 years) were enrolled in the study

major_points.text: Overall mortality numerically favored rate control, but was not statistically significant.
major_points.quote: mortality at five years, 23.8 percent and 21.3 percent, respectively; hazard ratio, 1.15 [95 percent confidence interval, 0.99 to 1.34]; P=0.08

major_points.text: Ischemic stroke rates were similar between groups and were about 1% per year.
major_points.quote: Ischemic strokes occurred in 77 and 80 patients in the rate-control and rhythm-control groups, respectively (Table 3), for an annual rate of approximately 1 percent per year in each group.

major_points.text: Most strokes occurred after warfarin discontinuation or with subtherapeutic INR.
major_points.quote: Most occurred in patients in whom warfarin had been stopped or in whom the INR was subtherapeutic.

inclusion_criteria.text: Patients who were at least 65 years of age or who had other risk factors for stroke or death could be enrolled.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who were at least 65 years of age or who had other risk factors for stroke or death could be enrolled in this study.

inclusion_criteria.text: Atrial fibrillation was likely to be recurrent (in the clinical judgment of the investigators).
inclusion_criteria.quote: The overriding criteria for enrollment were that (in the clinical judgment of the investigators) atrial fibrillation was likely to be recurrent;

criticisms.text: Results probably cannot be generalized to younger patients without risk factors for stroke (primary or “lone” atrial fibrillation).
criticisms.quote: Moreover, the results probably cannot be generalized to younger patients without risk factors for stroke (i.e., patients with primary, or “lone,” atrial fibrillation)

criticisms.text: Follow-up duration is years, but atrial fibrillation often requires treatment for decades; survival curves appeared to diverge later in follow-up.
criticisms.quote: Patients with atrial fibrillation often need treatment for decades, not years. However, the survival curves appear to be diverging, not converging, later in follow-up.

criticisms.text: Adverse effects of amiodarone might be expected to increase with longer use.
criticisms.quote: Furthermore, the adverse effects due to the most commonly used drug, amiodarone, might be reasonably expected to increase with longer use.

criticisms.text: The cardiac rhythm was classified only on the day of the follow-up visit, and atrial fibrillation could have been present at other times.
